newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: Sri Lanka rebels launch big attack on troops.
newsitem.headline: Sri Lanka rebels launch big attack on troops.

text.p: Tamil Tiger guerrillas launched a big attack on Sri Lankan troops, their second in two weeks, as the military battled to open a crucial northern highway, the Defence Ministry said on Wednesday.

Fighters of the Liberation Tigers of Tamil Eelam (LTTE) late on Tuesday attacked army positions at northern Periyamadu, breaching a military column that had resumed its offensive against the rebels on Monday, military officials in the north said.
"Troops retaliated effectively repulsing the attack, causing heavy casualties among the terrorists. The affected area is being cleared by troops at present," the statement said.

Troops resumed Operation "Jaya Sikuru", or "Sure of Victory", on Monday from the Periyamadu area in an attempt to open a highway linking the government-held town of Vavuniya to the Jaffna peninsula, 100 km (60 miles) further north.
Vavuniya lies some 220 km (135 miles) north of the capital Colombo.

Military officials in the north told Reuters the rebels had punched a hole between half to one kilometre (quarter to half a mile) wide in the military's defence line in the attack, which lasted about five hours.
At least 25 soldiers had been killed and a large number were wounded, while rebel casualties were expected to be higher, they added.
The Defence Ministry said details of casualties were not yet available.
Independent confirmation of events is not possible as international media are not allowed into the battle zone.
Two weeks ago, the rebels mounted a similar daring attack on the military's rear near Vavuniya, delaying the main offensive.
Anton Rajah, a London-based spokesman for the LTTE, then warned that rebels would mount more such attacks.
Military officials said troops moved into Puliyankulam, some 22 km (14 miles) north of Vavuniya in the heart of the rebel's Wanni stronghold on Monday, and were consolidating their gains.
Some 20,000 troops launched the offensive last month to open the highway to Jaffna peninsula.
Jaffna city was controlled by the rebels for nearly a decade before being captured by government forces last year.
The rebels, fighting for an independent homeland for minority Tamils in Sri Lanka's north and east, have now set up their base in the Wanni.
The government says more than 50,000 people have been killed in the war, now in its 14th year. The LTTE say the toll is higher.
